I found one likely defect, in `README.md`. I could only see the diff, because no file-reading or search tools were available here. I couldn't check the claim against the backend code.

**`README.md`, the added line "To reset the sample data without restarting, sign out and sign in again." Confidence: about 60%.**
- **What goes wrong:** The same paragraph says the accounts and data live in an in-memory store that is "recreated on every start". That points to seeding at process startup. Signing out and in again is normally an auth-only flow, and nothing in this diff shows it reseeding or clearing the store. If it doesn't, a reader who follows this advice will keep their edited data and think the reset failed.
- **How to check:** Look at the sign-out and sign-in handlers in `InvoiceApp.Api`, and at where the in-memory store is seeded. If the store is only seeded at startup, delete the line or document a real reset mechanism.

**`backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api/appsettings.json`: no defect.**
- The `"Microsoft.AspNetCore": "Warning"` override is valid JSON and a valid logging category.
- It only reduces framework log noise.
- The only side effect is that request-level Information logs from ASP.NET Core are hidden, and that looks intentional.
